description: Splits a polyphonic keyboard by pitch class: every one of the twelve notes gets its own gate output, and a switch says whether that note passes through to the main gate

inputs.text: Polyphonic pitch; the fraction of a volt on each channel picks which of the twelve keys that channel is using
Polyphonic gate; a channel above 5V counts as held, and a held note reaches the GATE output when its own switch is on

outputs.text: The gate voltage passed through for the channels whose note is switched on, and 0V for the rest

notes: nothing at all is written until a cable is patched to the pitch input; with it unpatched every output holds whatever voltage it last had.
with nothing patched to the gate input the pitch alone counts as held, so the twelve key gates follow the pitch and the GATE output stays at 0V.
the switches come up with the seven white keys on and the five black keys off, which passes a C major scale.
the twelve key gates carry a single voltage each: a note held on any channel raises its key gate, and nothing says which channel it came from.

inputs.0:
1V per octave · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.1:
high above 5V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the pitch alone counts as held; a negative voltage does nothing here.
